text:
Jesper Bratt was a 162nd overall pick in 2016 out of AIK, a player most of the league passed on. On Thursday his wrist shot 1:26 into overtime gave the Devils a 5-4 win over St. Louis and their third straight victory, and it capped a game NJD nearly let slip after leading 4-1.

The lead looked safe. Anthony Mantha scored twice, the second just 19 seconds after Jesper Boqvist's goal late in the second period, and Luke Hughes had opened the scoring. But St. Louis scored three times in the third, the last two 18 seconds apart: Philip Broberg's goal came on a 4% chance, and Dalibor Dvorsky tied it moments later. Mason McTavish also had a 42% look in overtime that Connor Hellebuyck turned away.

Our numbers say the Devils earned this one. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, favored NJD 6.59 to 4.04, and in a simulated replay of every shot they win 83% of the time. NJD took 67 shot attempts to STL's 51 and was well ahead early, 1.58 to 0.49 in the first period. Binnington saved about 1.6 goals more than his 36 shots against deserved, which is why the Blues were still in it. The Devils now carry three straight wins forward, while St. Louis leaves with a loss after a comeback that came up one shot short.
